sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the sequence from Rosh Hashanah through Sukkos, culminating in the future redemption and the universal service of G-d.

translations.translation: And this is the meaning of what is said, "In sukkos you shall dwell for seven days; every citizen in Israel shall dwell in sukkos,"
that after the service of "Blow the shofar in the month" on Rosh Hashanah,
when the drawing down is still in a manner of "in concealment,"
behold, after this come the ten days between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur, about which it is said,
"Seek G-d when He is found, call Him when He is near,"
and the saying of the Holy One, blessed be He, is considered an action,
and it becomes an action in actuality,
that "seek" and "call Him" are actualized in deed.
And this then effects the four days between Yom Kippur and Sukkos,
when the Torah of truth testifies that all of Israel and every individual Jew are occupied with mitzvos,
and after the preparation
(during these four days)
of "the festival of Sukkos you shall make for yourself" etc.
(with all the interpretations thereof)
[that even the making of the sukkah is included in the mitzvah,
as the Alter Rebbe writes in his Shulchan Aruch
to rule halachically regarding the reason for the ruling that we do not recite a blessing over its making because it is not the completion of the mitzvah,
and the blessing of Shehecheyanu also applies to the making]
behold, they then come on the festival of Sukkos to the fulfillment of the mitzvah itself,
"In sukkos you shall dwell for seven days."
And immediately the next morning
(at dawn and sunrise)
comes the mitzvah of the Four Species,

"And you shall take for yourselves on the first day the fruit of a beautiful tree, branches of date palms, and a branch of a leafy tree, and willows of the brook, and you shall rejoice before the L-rd your G-d."
Until they come to the Simchas Beis HaShoevah,
where the great joy of "and you shall rejoice" occurs in a manner of "whoever has not seen the Simchas Beis HaShoevah has never seen joy in his life."
And then they merit that very soon, "every citizen in Israel shall dwell in sukkos" will actually be fulfilled
(and not merely that they are fit to dwell),
for the true and complete redemption will come through our righteous Mashiach.
And then the fulfillment of the mitzvah of "and you shall rejoice before the L-rd your G-d" will be in completeness and from the Torah,
its fulfillment being in the Beis HaMikdash,
the third Beis HaMikdash,
"The Sanctuary, O L-rd, which Your hands have established,"
very soon.
He will come and redeem us and lead us upright to our land,
and build the Beis HaMikdash in its place,
and gather the dispersed of Israel, and the kingdom shall be the L-rd's.
And as an introduction to this, it will be as it is said,
"For then I will turn to the peoples a pure language, etc., to serve Him with one accord,"
which is drawn down in revelation through the offering of the seventy bulls on the festival of Sukkos.
May it be so for us,
and very soon.
